items.title: $223 Billion Back To Shareholders: Inside The MSFT Machine
items.summary: Microsoft handed shareholders one of the largest cash returns in market history, but what did that money actually buy for the owners who held on.

items.title: How Far Could CRM Stock Swing In A Year?
items.summary: Salesforce (CRM) stock trades at about $236 after returning about 58% over three months. Its options now price a range over roughly a year that runs from about $152 to about $368. The bottom of that band is a price the stock has already traded through within the past year, and the market is pricing the band a little calmer than the stock has actually moved.

items.title: Sandisk, Lennar, Viking Therapeutics, Shopify, GameStop, and More Stocks That Explain Today’s Market
items.summary: Sandisk rises. Rosenblatt initiates coverage of the stock with a Buy rating and a price target of $2,400.

items.title: Adobe Is Down 32% This Year: Is ADBE Stock Dead Money or Due for a Bounce?
items.summary: Adobe has fallen harder than its software peers while the broader market climbed, and the selling has not slowed even after quarterly results landed. The case for a bounce and the case for dead money both start with the same price chart and reach opposite conclusions.

items.title: Salesforce vs. ServiceNow: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: Salesforce offers a more attractive valuation and proven cash generation. ServiceNow offers faster growth and a more defensible market position.

items.title: 3 Big Tech Stocks With the Most Upside Right Now
items.summary: Wall Street has targets for Google, NVIDIA, and Salesforce, but one analyst thinks those numbers still leave serious money on the table heading into 2027. Here is the math behind three bold calls that could reshape how you size your tech positions.

items.title: The AI Software Story Wall Street Is Underrating
items.summary: Salesforce's agentic AI business is scaling at a pace that would make most enterprise software companies envious, yet the stock keeps getting priced like a relic from the CRM era. Something in that gap looks like an opportunity Wall Street has not yet caught up to.
